articles.title: Drupal Patches Critical Core RCE Flaw with No-Login Path via Contributed Modules
articles.content: Drupal core has a critical flaw in its Field UI module that could let an attacker run code on the site's server, and fixes were shipped on October 14 in Drupal 11.4.10, 11.3.19, and 10.6.19. An attacker cannot reach the flaw through core alone, the Drupal Security Team said in its advisory. Several exploit paths exist through contributed modules, and at least one known path needs no login.

articles.title: 双十一高性能游戏本大促：雷神猎刃 S 国补最高省 1500 元，i9-13900HX 搭配 RTX 5060
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，双十一到了，游戏本市场照例迎来一波集中促销，正是换机的好时机。目前雷神猎刃 S 的双十一活动已经开启，国补立减 15%，最多能省 1500 元。晒单还附赠雷神加速器季卡、休闲背包等权益；愿意再加 299 元的话，可以升级 3 年整机延保，并附上 Microsoft 365 个人版 3 个月订阅和 1TB 云存储空间。核心性能上，雷神猎刃 S 用的是英特尔酷睿 i9-13900HX：24 核心 32 线程，也就是 8 个性能核加 16 个能效核，最高睿频 5.4GHz，配 36MB 智能高速缓存。跑大型游戏、多开任务、做视频渲染，这颗 U 的算力都够用，规格放在当下依然能打。显卡则给到了 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU，Blackwell 架构，115W 满功耗释放，8GB GDDR7 显存、3328 个 CUDA 核心，AI 算力 572TOPS，支持 DLSS 5 与 Max-Q 技术。游戏渲染之外，这颗 GPU 的 AI 加速能力也能用在视频处理、图像生成这类创作场景里。散热方面，雷神猎刃 S 用了风驭散热架构：双涡流内吹设计负责理顺机身内部气流，再配合 3D 立体导热结构加快热量传导。官方数据是整机核心总功耗最高 185W，风扇最低噪音 43dB。屏幕是一块 16 英寸蜂鸟护眼 ADS Pro 屏，2.5K 分辨率、240Hz 刷新率，覆盖 100% DCI-P3 广色域，峰值亮度 500nit。对电竞玩家来说，高刷新率带来的动态画面明显更连贯；看电影、做创作，广色域加高亮度也接得住。护眼上，这块屏支持 DC 无频闪，还具备有害蓝光过滤能力，并通过了 A+ 规格认证，长时间盯着屏幕，眼睛的负担会小一些。扩展性上，机器预装 16GB DDR5 内存，双 SO-DIMM 插槽留好了，以后加内存也方便；硬盘是 1TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe 固态，双 M.2 硬盘位，支持 RAID 0/1。外观是典型的电竞风格：机身最薄处 23mm，A 面为阳极氧化金属材质，加 AF 防指纹工艺，机甲刻线、RGB 镜面 LOGO、侧边镭射铭牌这些元素一样不少，还支持 180° 开合。周边配置给得也比较全：80Wh 电池、140W 快充，随附 250W SiC 迷你适配器；全尺寸 RGB 背光键盘带独立方向键，触控板为类玻璃材质。独显直连、混合输出、核显输出三种显示模式可自由切换，WiFi 6、摄像头物理挡板也都安排上了。接口有 2.5G 网口、HDMI 2.1、Mini DP，以及多组 USB-A 和 USB-C，其中 USB-C 支持 PD 100W 充电和 140W 私有协议，3.5mm 音频接口与安全锁孔也都保留了下来。软件层面，雷神智控中心提供办公、游戏、狂暴三档性能模式，按使用场景切换即可，还支持可视化 UI BIOS 设置。京东雷神猎刃 S【RTX5060】 16 英寸学生游戏笔记本电脑（英特尔酷睿 i9HX RTX5060 16G1T）国家政府补贴国补后 8896 元起直达链接预算相对有限的话，机械师曙光 16S 青春版也值得一看。这是一台 AMD 平台游戏本，搭载锐龙 7 H255 处理器，8 核 16 线程，最高睿频 4.9GHz，显卡从 RTX 50 系列里选，其中 RTX 5060 版本配 8GB GDDR7 显存，主流游戏和部分创作场景都应付得来。它的屏幕是 16 英寸 2.5K 300Hz 高刷屏，100% sRGB 色域、500nit 亮度，电竞场景下刷新率更高、观感更顺滑。双 SO-DIMM 内存插槽加双 M.2 硬盘位，后期升级空间留得足；散热为双风扇四热管方案，并支持独显直连和双显三模切换。价格上，双十一叠加国补后，RTX 5050 版本到手 7819.15 元起，RTX 5060 版本 8329.15 元起。预算在 7 千到 8 千之间、想买 AMD 平台高性能游戏本的话，可以看看它，当作雷神猎刃 S 之外的另一个选项。天猫机械师曙光 16S 青春版 【直播间闪降 300+ 国补 15%】锐龙 7 H 255 RTX5060/5050 16 英寸学生电竞游戏本笔记本电脑国补后 8074 元起直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 我国渤海海域 5G 网络覆盖率超 80%，综合信号覆盖率 95%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，由交通运输部北海航海保障中心联合中海石油有限公司天津分公司、中国移动通信集团天津有限公司建设的渤海海域通信感知网今日正式开通运行，综合信号覆盖率达 95%，5G 网络覆盖率超 80%，渤海主要港口、锚地和航路航道实现信号全覆盖。这意味着渤海全面进入高速互联、全域感知的新阶段，各类涉海活动将获得高速、稳定、可靠的宽带通信和实时感知服务。据介绍，该项目新建 48 座 5G 基站、8 座 VHF 基站、6 座 AIS 基站和 4 座水文观测站，与原有岸基、海基网络有机交织。海上没有电线杆，陆地基站依托铁塔光纤的模式在海上无法复制。IT之家注意到，渤海拥有 300 多座石油平台，项目从中精选 48 座，在平台上架设 5G 基站，利用平台原有海底光缆回传信号到陆地，如同在海上建起一座座“海上服务区”，船舶进入覆盖范围即可上网。据央视新闻报道，项目选用 700MHz 频段作为 5G 覆盖的核心频段。该频段因覆盖范围广、穿透能力强、传输损耗低，在业界被称为“黄金频段”。在海上环境中，其优势尤为突出：单基站海上覆盖可达 40 公里，而采用高频方案则需 15 座基站才能达到同等覆盖效果，700MHz 仅需 2 座，大幅节省建设成本；波长较长带来的强绕射能力，使船舱等遮挡位置也能收到信号；信号损耗小、设备功耗低的特点，则既能满足手机上网需求，也可长期支撑海上各类监测传感器工作。这套系统并非单一网络的堆砌，而是多种通信感知手段的协同。AIS 如同眼睛，实时上报船舶位置、航速、航向；VHF 如同嘴巴和耳朵，实现船岸、船船对讲与险情一键呼叫；5G 如同信息高速公路，支持上网、视频通话和监控画面回传；水文观测站如同皮肤，24 小时监测潮位、水流和水温，感知海洋环境变化。四者协同，构成了渤海全域“看得见、听得到、传得回”的通信感知体系。在民生层面，这张网的价值直接可感。辽鲁航线是国内最繁忙的跨渤海客滚运输通道，年运输旅客近 500 万人次，乘船旅客在航行途中可随时与家人报平安。渔民出海可接收气象预警，遇险时快速求救。海上平台作业的监控与生产数据也能实时回传陆地，提升作业效率。据新华社，2025 年 12 月 21 日，渤海南部海域首座石油平台 5G 示范基站建成开通，经测试可满足电话、微信、视频通话等通信需求，此后项目进入全面推广阶段，至今年 10 月 15 日实现全域开通。安全保障层面的改善尤为显著。过去渤海中部是通信盲区，船舶“看不见、喊不应”，搜救难度大。如今 AIS 基站覆盖 95% 海域，船舶动态可实时掌握；8 座 VHF 基站保障应急呼叫直达交管中心；5G 网络实现视频与位置回传，支撑救援精准调度；虚拟航标划定海上航道，引导商渔船分道航行以减少碰撞。

articles.title: 英伟达发布 617.70 热修复驱动，修复 G-SYNC Pulsar 320 FPS 限制及黑屏闪烁问题
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，英伟达今日发布了 GeForce 617.70 热修复驱动，针对 360Hz 高刷显示器上出现的两项问题进行了修复。该驱动基于 GeForce 617.42 WHQL 正式版构建，仅包含针对性的代码调整，不通过 NVIDIA App 自动分发，用户需前往官方下载服务器手动获取安装包。此次热修复主要解决 G-SYNC Pulsar 显示器上帧率被限制在 320 FPS 的问题，以及 QHD 分辨率下 360Hz 显示器在游戏中出现短暂黑屏闪烁的问题。据英伟达介绍，部分支持 G-SYNC Pulsar 技术的 360Hz 显示器在游戏中，帧率会自发下降至约 320 FPS，同时输入延迟明显增加。IT之家注：G-SYNC Pulsar 是英伟达今年 1 月推出的新一代动态清晰度技术，通过在显示器背光上进行脉冲控制，结合可变刷新率，实现超过 1000Hz 感知的有效动态清晰度。该技术采用区域背光脉冲方案，将背光划分为多个水平分区，以自上而下的顺序逐行脉冲点亮，脉冲周期为一帧时间的 25%。当显示器以 360Hz 运行时，帧率被错误限制在 320 FPS，意味着 Pulsar 的脉冲时序与帧输出节奏之间出现了错位。英伟达此前已确认定位到问题根因，并在本次热修复中予以解决。第二个问题主要涉及 QHD 分辨率下 360Hz 显示器在游戏过程中偶发的短暂黑屏闪烁。该问题主要影响 GeForce RTX 30 和 RTX 40 系列显卡，受影响显示器会短暂丢失画面，但游戏本身仍在继续运行。英伟达表示，617.70 驱动仅修复了部分黑屏情况，公司仍在继续调查其余案例。对于仍然遇到黑屏闪烁的用户，英伟达建议在 NVIDIA 控制面板中将电源管理模式设置为“最大性能优先”作为临时解决方案，更改设置后需要重启系统。除此之外，还有一项已知问题尚未解决：显示器从睡眠模式唤醒后，G-SYNC 和 G-SYNC Pulsar 可能变为不可用。英伟达表示已在内部复现该问题，但尚未公布修复时间表。IT之家附英伟达下载地址：https://international.download.nvidia.com/Windows/617.70hf/617.70-desktop-notebook-win10-win11-64bit-international-dch.hf.exe

articles.title: 英伟达黄仁勋盛赞 OpenClaw 助力机器人技术发展，但权限管控必须得有
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据科技媒体 TechRadar 今天报道，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋近期在伦敦的 Build a Claw 活动认为，OpenClaw 将推动未来科技发展，特别是机器人领域。黄仁勋首先指出，OpenClaw 是迄今为止最重要的模型之一，有助于多个行业进步。他对此解释称：“我们已经看到人工智能迎来转折点，它开始变得实用。人们正在用 AI 做各种事情，从简单的软件编程，到担任营销代理、研究助理和实验室助理、药物研发，如今到处都有智能体。”IT之家从原报道获悉，黄仁勋看到合作伙伴 Humanoid 的机器人后认为，OpenClaw 是“首个真正可信的智能体运行框架”。他认为 OpenClaw 就像外骨骼的大语言模型，应用在机器人领域可能带来许多好处。他说道：“OpenClaw 刚推出时，我就觉得它是非常出色的数字机器人系统。它有点像具身智能，本质是为 LLM 提供了实时运行框架。电机、关节、车轮和机械臂都只是工具，最终要由电脑运行的智能体操控。”“这种情况与互联网早期很相似。当时浏览器并未与计算机隔离，用户访问网站时，这些 Web 页面可能会下载应用程序，并获得对底层硬件的完全控制权，而且还会向用户的电脑推送它所说的「特殊软件包」。”“最显而易见的解决方法就是建立容器，也就是隔离层，本质上是在操作系统内部再运行一个 OS。因此我们开发了 OpenShell 系统。当你开发一个自主系统时，首先应该假设任何对象都不可信，仅授予最低权限。例如你让一个自主系统做煎蛋，就没必要给它电锯，它只需要一口煎锅。”关于 AI 智能体失控的论调，黄仁勋比较乐观，他认为权限管控是必要的：“我们会持续监控这些自主系统。如果机器人违反规则，或者做出超出权限范围的行动，系统就会发出警报。我们可以决定是否让它闭嘴。”

articles.title: 《雾锁王国》1.0 正式版发售：Steam 国区 138 元，完整地图解锁
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，《雾锁王国》（Enshrouded）结束近三年的抢先体验阶段，1.0 正式版今日正式上线，登陆 PC（Steam）和 PlayStation 5 平台（PS5 与 PS5 Pro 版本目标 60 帧运行），但 Xbox Series X|S 版本已推迟至 2027 年春季。据 Keen Games 官方公告，Xbox 版延期是因开发团队认为需要额外时间才能达到其期望的质量与性能表现。IT之家注：1.0 版本首发暂不支持跨平台联机，开发团队表示正在为此努力，但暂无法预估所需时间。国区定价方面，Steam 标准版售价 138 元，原声音乐 28 元，游戏支持简体中文。据 Steam 商店页面信息，1.0 版对旧存档完全兼容，玩家无需重新开始。不过需要注意的是，所有角色的技能树将在首次进入 1.0 版本时被重置，自定义按键绑定也会恢复默认设置，因为 1.0 新增了大量控制选项。抢先体验期间参与游戏的玩家将获得专属奖励。1.0 版本最核心的内容是完整地图的解锁。新区域“余烬摇篮”位于北方，穿过帷幕水盆地后开启的大门即可进入。该区域分为上下两层：下层是熔岩流淌的荒芜之地，散落着神秘过往的遗迹，部分地区被瘴气吞噬；上层则是远古人抬升大地后打造的浮空岛屿国度，充满奇特生物、精巧建筑和毫不留情的守护者。两层世界之间由不断向上蔓延的瘴气触须相连。此外，阿尔班耶夫山脉和帷幕水盆地各新增一座空荡礼堂，春日平原、黑沼和燃火荒原等既有生态区域也向世界边缘大幅扩展。等级与成长系统随之扩展。玩家等级上限从抢先体验版的 45 级提升至 50 级，装备最高可升级至 55 级。火焰祭坛数量上限提升至 15 座，击败最终 Boss 后还可额外解锁一个火焰等级，使火焰祭坛能在过去无法触及的瘴气区域绽放。一位精通远古知识与配方的新幸存者将加入玩家基地，解锁新一阶的制作内容，包括新装备、工具、食物、消耗品、箭矢与法术，以及新的家具、摆件、建筑方块和植物。战斗系统的调整是 1.0 的另一重点。法师职业获得显著加强，共新增 9 种法术：吸取法力（Mana Drain）、缠绕（Entangle）、烈焰之柱（Pillar of Flames）、暴风雪（Blizzard）、球状闪电（Ball Lightning），以及四种全新的召唤法术 —— 火焰图腾、寒冰图腾、电击图腾和空洞骷髅。召唤法术是 1.0 引入的全新法术类别，技能树中新增了两个技能用于提升可召唤的骷髅和图腾数量。魔杖战斗也得到重做，新增重击攻击，可穿透敌人并打断弱敌的攻击动作；同时加入空中魔杖攻击和魔杖闪避攻击两项新技能。永恒法术（不消耗法术弹药）现在可以像武器和护甲一样升级，获得独特的新增益效果。基地建造系统新增 Sparkworks 逻辑系统，玩家可以用它制作可互动的内容，并通过分享平台交流。该系统的完整版本扩展了陷阱、生成器和逻辑元件，理论上允许玩家在游戏中构建自定义地牢。世界中所有的背景故事笔记、信件和书籍现在提供完整的英文、德文和中文配音，玩家可以像听有声书一样收听背景故事，还能将多篇笔记加入播放列表依次播放。据 Keen Games 创意总监 Antony Christoulakis 透露，游戏玩家数已超过 500 万。该作于 2024 年 1 月 24 日进入 Steam 抢先体验，四天内售出 100 万份，同年 8 月销量超过 300 万份，鼎盛时期 Steam 同时在线玩家数达到 160,405 人。

articles.title: 海光信息 2026 年三季度归母净利润 27.1~29.8 亿元，预计同比增长 38.16%~51.93%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，海光信息今日发布 2026 年三季度（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 9 月）业绩预告报告：营业总收入：142.8 亿元 ~155.8 亿元，预计同比增长 50.47%~64.17%归母净利润：27.1 亿元 ~29.8 亿元，预计同比增长 38.16%~51.93%扣非净利润：24.5 亿元 ~27.1 亿元，预计同比增长 34.86%~49.17% AI 解读本次业绩预告营收和净利润增速均大幅高于市场预期，表现超预期。公司主营业务说明海光信息主要从事研发、设计和销售应用于服务器、工作站等计算、存储设备中的高端处理器，产品包括海光通用处理器 (CPU) 和海光协处理器 (DCU)，产品广泛应用于电信、金融、互联网等多个行业。本次财报业绩亮点预计 2026 年前三季度实现营业收入 142.8 亿元到 155.8 亿元，同比增长 50.47% 到 64.17% ，营收规模同比接近翻倍增长；预计实现归属于母公司所有者的净利润 27.1 亿元到 29.8 亿元，同比增长 38.16% 到 51.93% ，净利润保持高速增长；预计实现归属于母公司所有者的扣除非经常性损益的净利润 24.5 亿元到 27.1 亿元，同比增长 34.86% 到 49.17% ，扣非后增速同样保持高位。业绩增长主要原因受人工智能产业快速发展、国产化进程由政策驱动全面转向市场驱动等因素带动，国内高端芯片需求持续攀升。报告期内，公司牢牢把握发展机遇期，持续优化“CPU+DCU”业务布局，围绕通用计算和人工智能计算市场，加大研发投入力度、迭代优化产品性能，市场竞争力不断增强，实现了公司业绩的持续增长。风险提示本次预告数据为初步核算数据，具体准确的财务数据以公司正式披露的 2026 年第三季度报告为准，投资者需注意投资风险。相关阅读： 《中科曙光 2026 年三季度归母净利润 17.24 亿元，同比增长 78.48%》《江波龙 2026 年三季度归母净利润 140~149 亿元，同比增长 1864.55%~1990.84%》《复旦微电 2026 年三季度归母净利润 9.5 亿元 ~11.5 亿元，同比 187.63%~248.18%》《台积电 2026 财年第三财季归母净利润 7630.64 亿新台币，同比增长 68.7%》《阿斯麦 2026 财年第三财季归母净利润 49.6 亿欧元，同比增长 133.49%》《海光信息 2026 年半年度归母净利润 17.98 亿元，同比增长 49.69%》《海光信息 2026 年半年度归母净利润 17 亿元～ 18.3 亿元，同比增长 41.50%~52.32%》风险提示：本文内容由 AI 自动分析生成，仅供参考，不代表IT之家观点。如有出入请以证监会指定上市公司信息披露平台为准。本文内容不构成投资建议，如有投资者据此操作，风险自担，IT之家对此不承担任何责任。

articles.title: SK 海力士推出 3D FeNAND 技术，瞄准 AI 计算
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据韩媒 The Elec 今天报道，SK 海力士现已公布 3D FeNAND 实现模拟存内计算（Analog Compute-in-Memory，A-CiM）的研究成果，相关研究已发表于 IEEE 论文。据介绍，A-CiM 可利用模拟信号直接在存储器执行乘积累加运算（IT之家注：MAC），减少数据搬运、提升处理速度和能效。3D FeNAND 则利用铁电材料的极化状态存储数据并控制电流。对比之下，传统 3D NAND 采用电荷俘获氮化物（CTN）结构，将电子捕获在氮化物层中。铁电材料的特点是，即使外部电场消失，其内部极化状态仍能保持。SK 海力士表示，FeNAND 可在单个存储单元内产生多种电流状态，适合 AI 计算所需的权重数据。

articles.title: How are you centralising AI for development at your company?
articles.content:
I'm asking this because I'm seeing some frustrating patterns and if I may be bold, I think my answer is the correct one.Here's one I'm seeing: its the SDLC agent pattern and I think its wrong.Step 1: you have good AGENTS.md documentation for your code and other principles. (this is good)Step 2: There's a somewhat strict workflow and steps enforced like planner agent, reviewer agent, critique agent and directly create a PR from a ticket. Every human intervention here is considered an anti-pattern.I'd like it to be as simple as having documentation and giving developer full freedom with choice of harness, tools (MCP) and just make the pull request.What's the logic behind the multi step planner, reviewer, critique agents?

Abstract: Under the accelerated pace of AI development, any benchmark whose difficulty is calibrated with humans or current AI systems becomes circular, or saturates soon. Abstract: Large language models have significantly lowered the barrier to writing code. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14136v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Iterative sampling in diffusion models can lead to error accumulation due to exposure bias. The denoiser is trained on real images interpolated with noise, but at inference its inputs are constructed from its own imperfect predictions from the earlier steps, something it has never seen at training time. Abstract: Organisations that want language-model agents for security work face a choice between open-weight models, which they can run and audit themselves, and far more expensive closed frontier models. articles.title: Visualizing the World Model in an Agent's Value Function
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14186v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Could model-free reinforcement learning algorithms actually be learning a model of the environment? In this work, we apply counterfactual interventions which hold everything about a state fixed, besides a targeted change, to explore if the value function of a Proximal Policy Optimization agent forms a world model of the Crafter environment. Despite only being trained to optimize reward, we discover that the value function learns concepts such as the rules governing when a diamond is collectible, water and food having an impact on health, heuristics regarding inventory, and more. Finally, we discuss the safety implications of our visualizations and some shortcomings of current reinforcement learning agents that will prevent us from building truly advanced machine intelligence.

articles.title: Should SLMs be in the Driver's Seat? A Study of Local Models as Interpreters in Cloud-Written Agent Programs
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14209v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The most accurate agents executing user-provided tasks are driven by large, cloud-hosted models, which solve them by reading the private data of the user. Agents powered by models small enough to run on edge devices keep that data local, but yield far worse results. A third option is to have cloud models write a program that devices execute: the data stays local, but as the program is written before any data is seen, it fails whenever a step depends on interpreting content that appears only at run time. We explore an intermediate architecture, in which the cloud-written program defers bounded questions over user data to a small local model through an ordinary function call. On AppWorld this improves the success rate of a code-only agent in all six combinations of backbone model and test partition we evaluate, by up to 14.9pp, recovering a substantial part of the gap to a cloud-hosted ReAct loop while keeping user data on the device.

Abstract: LLM agents' capabilities depend not only on their underlying models but also on their execution harnesses. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising approach to automatically evolve these harnesses. However, deploying RSI in open-world settings still faces two critical challenges. First, open-world tasks are typically unseen during the harness design phase and novel at test time, leaving no ground-truth verifiers to reliably guide online harness edits. Second, the RSI process remains highly task-specific and fails to generalize to novel scenarios. We introduce Harness^2, a plug-and-play, recursive agent harnessing framework that addresses these challenges through two connected levels of recursion. Task-level recursion refines the current task's harness using a contrastive Propose-Probe-Compose step that reliably guides edits without ground-truth verifiers, and can be scaled further via parallel or sequential recursion. articles.title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14277v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tensor parallelism ends every layer with an all-reduce that sits between two dependent matrix multiplications, so its cost cannot be hidden and grows as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth. Sending 4-bit instead of 16-bit values would cut this cost by nearly 4x, but the all-reduce must add the values it carries, and rounding the sum injects an error at every call. Model quality depends on how these errors accumulate over layers, yet existing methods treat each call on its own. We present Echo, a 4-bit all-reduce for training and inference that controls the accumulated error. Echo moves data in 4 bits and sums in high precision, so each value is quantized at most twice per call for any number of GPUs. The summation reveals each injected error, and Echo feeds it back into later calls, so old errors cancel instead of accumulating. articles.title: Controllable Diverse Sampling through Pullback Directions
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14294v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conditional diffusion models can generate high-quality images that align closely with a given prompt. However, samples generated from different random seeds may remain visually similar, limiting creative exploration. Existing approaches can increase variation, but often require additional optimization or sampling overhead, while stronger perturbations may introduce distortions that degrade image quality or prompt alignment. We propose a training-free method that leverages the local pullback geometry induced by the mapping from the conditioning-embedding space to the image space to identify directions of maximal output sensitivity. By steering different sampling trajectories along these directions, we encourage distinct generations while maintaining consistency with the conditioning signal. Experiments on MS-COCO and BrushNet show the efficacy of the method in improving diversity on prompt-conditioned image generation and inpainting.

Abstract: Benchmark scores tell us what an LLM can do, but not how much energy is required to deliver that capability. arXiv:2610.18877v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-series language models typically align numerical signals with language using labels, captions, or question-answer pairs. Although such supervision encourages linguistic representations, it does not explicitly require them to preserve information about how the underlying time-series signal evolves. We introduce forecast grounding, a pretraining principle that requires language-aligned time-series representations to remain predictive of the future evolution before they are adapted to downstream tasks. We instantiate this principle in LOTUS, which divides each time-series channel into non-overlapping patches and maps them into the LLM embedding space. Abstract: Post-training reasoning LLMs often requires making a tradeoff between costly supervision and compute inefficiency: supervised finetuning typically requires reasoning traces, which is data inefficient since in many applications one only has prompt-answer tuples and lacks the groundtruth chain-of-thought (CoT) sequence. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.18880v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-throughput perturbation screens increasingly use machine-learning models to predict the effects of gene combinations that were never measured. A difficult case arises when both genes in a test pair were seen individually during training, but their combination was not. In this setting, standard OOD methods often fail because neither gene appears unfamiliar on its own. We therefore compare each model prediction with a simple additive prediction obtained by summing the two observed single-gene effects. The difference between them, which we call additive disagreement (AD), measures how much extra interaction effect the model introduces for an unseen combination. Abstract: Token-selection methods for on-policy distillation (OPD) prioritize student-visited positions using diverse signals, including uncertainty, teacher-student disagreement, and mismatch direction. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19013v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Current scaling law formulations suggest that increasing the number of unique samples in a dataset improves model performance, while repeated exposure to the same samples provides diminishing value. Abstract: Real measurements are too limited to train an accurate indoor pathloss predictor that works across a wide range of buildings. Large-scale synthetic pretraining offers a way forward, but real building layouts are also scarce, and accurate ray-tracing simulators are slow, expensive, and often proprietary. articles.title: Lag: A Mean-Field Optimal Policy for Online Assignment with Reusable Resources
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19038v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study online task assignment with reusable resources. This problem arises in peer reviewer assignment, skill-based call routing, rideshare matching, emergency dispatch, and crowdsourcing: Tasks arrive according to a geometric process and must be immediately assigned to servers that become temporarily busy, yielding rewards that depend on the task-server pair. The goal is to maximize long-run average reward.
  We cast the problem as a contextual restless multi-armed bandit (CRMAB). We derive an occupancy-measure LP (OCC-LP) that upper-bounds the reward of any work-conserving policy. From its dual we obtain Lag, a closed-form index policy. We introduce a scaling regime in which the number of copies of each server and the number of arrivals per step grow together. This regime yields the first deterministic fluid limit for a contextual bandit. In it, Lag is asymptotically optimal.

Abstract: Understanding the mechanism behind why diffusion models memorize their training data remains an open question in generative modeling. In this paper, we examine this question from two perspectives: (a) the model-level perspective concerning the onset of memorization in a model during training, and (b) the sample-level perspective concerning the proclivity of an individual sample to be memorized by a given model. We show that the so-called input loss curvature, or the Frobenius norm of the Hessian of the diffusion model's training loss, is an effective metric for quantifying both perspectives on memorization. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19046v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Information-theoretic exploration is of primary interest in methodological studies of reinforcement learning (RL) and computational cognitive neuroscience, while the established RL theory builds regret guarantees on confidence sets. This situation leaves open the conditions under which the information-driven exploration found in nature is more advantageous than the exploration of the established RL theory. We put the state-of-the-art methods of these two paradigms, Active Inference (AIF) and Bayes-UCBVI, on an equal footing: both act through the same state abstraction of a tabular MDP with $S$ states, and their greedy forms differ only in the exploration term. We find that AIF's information gain decays too fast to serve as a confidence width, locking greedy agents that explore by it out of the optimal action. Abstract: Recent work has questioned whether large language models (LLMs) can be useful for temporal event prediction. Abstract: Science fiction is widely credited with unsettling gender. This article asks whether that holds at the linguistic level, in how readily gendered reference gives way to its counterpart, a neutral term, or other social category, and whether it separates the genre from general fiction. articles.title: Pre-Trained Language Models as Zero-Shot Tools for Social Science Research
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19048v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Record linkage and demographic inference from names are routine demands in social science. Most approaches to these problems require labeled training data that are difficult or costly to acquire. I show that pre-trained language models perform both tasks accurately without requiring task-specific training. For record linkage, I introduce EnsembleLink, an algorithm that uses pre-trained embeddings alongside string-based scorers to retrieve a short list of candidates and then identify the likeliest matches. EnsembleLink matches or exceeds the performance of most prior approaches while generalizing across scripts and formats that those methods are unable to handle. For ethnicity inference from names, I show that large language models (LLMs) achieve up to 83.8% accuracy on U.S. voter files, compared to 78.0% for name-supplemented BISG. articles.title: Similar Models, Broken Odds: Where Luce's Axiom Fails in Chatbot Arena
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19095v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chatbot Arena ranks language models with the Bradley-Terry model, which gives each model one score and so assumes Luce's choice axiom. Choice theory predicts where this fails: near-copies are told apart more decisively than their scores imply. On 1.8 million Arena votes, votes between versions of one model are 1.37 times as decisive as Bradley-Terry predicts, between sizes of one generation 1.26 times and between models of one lab 1.12 times; a release a year later gives consistent multipliers, and the effect survives alternative tie treatments, prompt subsets and topics, and timing checks. How alike two models' answers are worded and formatted tracks the effect. articles.title: From Copying to Composition: How Language Models Develop In-Context Learning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19113v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) allows language models to adapt their behavior from instructions and demonstrations in a prompt, but accuracy alone does not reveal how contextual information controls their predictions. We study the acquisition and trainability of ICL with a controlled diagnostic that separates copying a nearby demonstration from integrating information across the prompt. Across 17 models, about a third prefer the copied answer, a few are undecided, and the rest prefer the rule-consistent answer, which goes with higher accuracy and with control by the requested value rather than the closest conflicting example. Checkpoint analyses show that models begin prioritizing task-relevant prompt tokens over conflicting examples long before their accuracy improves beyond chance level. articles.title: DecisionRobust: Benchmarking Robustness for JEV Style Decision Models Across Text and Vision
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19118v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Emerging decision models such as JEV provide typed interfaces that map task instructions and observations directly to choices, judgments, and scores. As these models are increasingly used for automated decision-making, understanding their reliability under adversarial manipulation becomes critical. We introduce DecisionRobust, a benchmark for systematically evaluating the robustness of decision models across textual and visual inputs. Our benchmark covers practical decision-making scenarios and a diverse suite of attacks, including semantics-preserving text perturbations, image perturbations, and prompt injection in both modalities. We curate evaluation sets through external validity checks and cross-model candidate selection. We evaluate 30 model configurations on text tasks and 17 on vision tasks, including 24 and 12 held-out models, respectively, that are excluded from candidate selection. Our experiments reveal several key findings.

articles.title: CAFE: Confining Feature Distillation to Language-Routed Adapters for Compact Multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19134v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Feature distillation is usually expected to add to logit distillation. We find that this expectation does not hold for two common feature losses in compact multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR), and analyze why through their gradients. The gradient of a projection-based loss is orthogonal to the task gradient, while that of Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA), a similarity-based loss, is weakly aligned with it. CKA lowers the word error rate (WER) on non-English languages, but at the expense of data-rich English. Three loss-level remedies (one trained, two probed) all fall short, and the CKA gradient overlaps with the subspace English uses in the shared encoder by 97.5% to 99.5% (about 81% by chance). Guided by this diagnosis, we propose CAFE (Confined-Adapter Feature distillation), which confines the CKA gradient to adapters that English bypasses, addressing the trade-off in the parameters rather than in the loss. articles.title: From Qualitative Text to Integrated Evidence: The Parallel-Then-Integrated (PTI) Procedure
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19164v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mixed methods research offers established strategies for integrating qualitative and quantitative evidence, but less guidance for integrating two computational representations of the same qualitative corpus. This methodological study introduces Parallel-Then-Integrated (PTI), a four-step procedure for explicit and traceable integration. We present PTI using 1,203 interview paragraphs from 29 mothers in Nepal. The two representations were ontology-guided Patient Voice (PV) coding with PVminer and data-driven themes generated through non-negative matrix factorization (NMF). A theme-complete crosswalk documented convergence, divergence, and preprocessing-sensitive differences. Depression status, based on Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores, served as a secondary external anchor for exploratory association checks. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19166v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Meta-evaluation of text generation metrics and LLM-judges is primarily conducted using metric-human correlations. However, prior work has shown that correlation is not an appropriate estimate of a metric's evaluation capability and can be unstable across evaluation settings, such as different datasets or languages. Therefore, we propose a regression-based meta-evaluation of metrics that learns on calibrated metric outputs to predict human ratings. We ground this measurement relative to a trivial constant-mean baseline and human agreements to provide a comparable measure of metric capability across evaluation settings. To test our meta-evaluation framework, we developed a large-scale multi-lingual style-personalized text generation (SPTG) benchmark, collecting multiple annotations across 10 topologically diverse languages and four evaluation dimensions, each with varying degrees of subjectivity. articles.title: HERO: Harnessing Evidence for Test-time Refinement and Prompt Optimization in Program Generation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19184v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Harness optimization improves LLMs by refining reusable prompts and scaffolding, yet requires further adaptation for program generation tasks such as text-to-SQL and text-to-Python. Existing methods often rely on LLM reflectors to propose harness updates, which can fix observed failures but also disrupt previously correct behavior. Text-to-code tasks offer a natural way to mitigate this issue: we can execute generated outputs, allowing us to evaluate and verify the effects of proposed updates directly. Building on this signal, we introduce \textsc{HERO} (\textbf{H}arnessing \textbf{E}vidence for \textbf{R}efinement and \textbf{O}ptimization), which combines offline and test-time harness optimization. At the first stage, \method{} learns reusable prompt updates from execution-verified successes and failures and validates candidate revisions before adoption. articles.title: How to Evaluate When You Don't Know How to Evaluate? Choosing Reliable Setups for Base Language Model Benchmarking
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19185v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluation of large language models (LLMs) remains largely pre-scientific: it involves many design decisions, with little guidance on how to make them. These choices can substantially affect measured performance and, consequently, decisions about subsequent pretraining. To identify effective evaluation setups, we investigate 8 aspects, such as task formulation or the number of in-context examples. We compare the setups using three widely-used signal criteria, repurposed as normative meta-measures: monotonicity, non-randomness, and ranking consistency of the evaluation scores across intermediate checkpoints. In an early pretraining scenario, we evaluate these setups on 26 monolingual 2B-parameter models trained on different types of data, using 80 tasks in four languages. articles.title: NEPSEE: A Double-Annotated Benchmark for Nepali Sentiment Analysis
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19190v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many sentiment datasets use one annotator for each item, so the test labels show the conventions of that person. We build a Nepali benchmark from two annotators who labelled the same sentences blind. They labelled 5,614 sentences from tweets of Nepali public figures on a five-point scale. We keep only the 3,189 sentences where both give the same polarity. On the three-class benchmark, NepBERTa with a fixed tokenizer gets a macro-F1 of 0.877 and IndicBERTv2 0.867. Three commercial large language models (LLMs) get 0.882 to 0.896 zero-shot, and these differences are not significant. On the five-point scale, 766 sentences have two adjacent labels, for example Pos and SPos. We accept both labels and train on both. On this task, Claude Opus 5.5 beats the best encoders by 0.10 to 0.12 macro-F1. A tokenizer audit adds a second result. The default tokenizers of three Nepali BERT models delete the non-spacing Devanagari vowel signs and the virama.

articles.title: Weighted Ensemble Sampling for Rare-Event Estimation in Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19202v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rare but severe failures of large language models can become practically significant at deployment scale. Estimating their probabilities with direct Monte Carlo sampling is highly inefficient, while proposal-based methods typically require auxiliary learning of an additional proposal distribution. We introduce \textbf{Weighted Ensemble (WE)}, a training-free framework for rare-event estimation in language models. WE samples exclusively from the original language model and improves upon direct Monte Carlo by periodically reallocating the sampling budget toward prefixes that appear more likely to reach the target rare event. To guide this reallocation without learning a separate proposal distribution, we exploit internal LLM representations as prefix-level signals and empirically validate their effectiveness. articles.title: DUALVIEW: Leveraging Broad and Output-Specific Evidence for LLM-based Multi-Output Text Regression
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19206v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While work on LLM-based regression has largely focused on scalar prediction, multi-output text regression remains less explored. We present DualView, a parameter-efficient approach to leverage LLMs for multi-output text regression. \method{} first extracts broad and output-specific representations from a frozen LLM, then uses a dual-branch architecture to produce the full score vector. Across five heterogeneous regression tasks and eight LLMs (up to 122B), DualView outperforms seven supervised regression baselines while requiring 82--1842 times fewer fitted parameters than the three strongest baselines. These improvements extend across individual output dimensions and persist even with limited training data. Notably, DualView using a smaller open-weight LLM can outperform unsupervised prediction with Gemini 3.1 Pro. articles.title: Titan-Llama: Retrofitting Pre-trained LLMs with External Neural Memory Modules
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Transformers are efficient to pre-train at scale because attention permits parallel computation across sequence positions, but long-context inference requires increasingly large KV caches. Efficient recurrent alternatives reduce the asymptotic complexity of inference, but their sequential dependence limits token-wise parallelism during training, making them harder to scale. Further, the current paradigm of extending long context tasks creates competing notions of retaining information precisely and keeping long-context inference efficient. To address this gap, we introduce Titan-Llama, a post-training method for retrofitting attention-based language models with a hierarchical memory architecture that updates parameters at test-time. Titan-Llama applies a blockwise attention mask and preserves full-fidelity attention over recent tokens while compressing historical context into recurrent, fixed-size neural memory modules (NMMs). articles.title: Do Syntax Heads Influence Model Behavior?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19231v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Transformer language models develop attention heads that specialize in syntactic relations, for example, attending from verbs to their subjects. Do these heads play a causal role in the model's syntactic predictions? Evidence for such a role is mixed to negative: even when we force these heads to attend to a distractor noun other than the subject, the model's syntactic predictions are still more consistent with the subject than with the distractor. Interventions on specialized syntax heads had a significantly stronger effect on syntactic predictions than interventions on random heads, but only in one of the two measures we propose.

articles.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19247v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Transformers are intuitively considered to be efficient at copying from their inputs. We actually show that the ability of LLMs to copy in context can be improved through explicit modeling. We propose Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLMs), which add a lightweight Copy-Paste head to the conventional language modeling (LM) head. CPLMs improve training efficiency, downstream performance, and offer new operating points in long-context and retrieval setups. We validate our approach by pretraining models from 135M to 1.7B parameters, showing improvements across all scales and backbones with negligible training and inference overheads. We explain the success of CPLMs by showing that they partially mitigate the LM head gradient bottleneck through an alternative gradient path.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19007v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: World models are a powerful means of reasoning and planning, but many of these action-conditioned predictive models are high dimensional and computationally expensive. These challenges limit the number of action candidates that can be evaluated by a planner. We show that this cost is avoidable for planners over short horizons, which only require local information with respect to the current state. For a fixed state, the frames reachable by varying a low-dimensional action (a camera movement or an end-effector command) lie on a low-dimensional manifold. We estimate the local shape of that manifold directly via a network trained to estimate how each image region moves per unit of each action axis supervised by data collected from samples by the generator. articles.title: How Far Can Coding Agents Go in Visual Generation?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19025v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern image generation largely relies on specialized generative models that leave the process of image construction implicit in learned parameters. We explore an alternative: general-purpose coding agents that construct images through executable programs. Our study of zero-shot drawing on AgentDrawBench, a 200-prompt benchmark, reveals a distinctive capability profile. Agents excel at preserving structure and satisfying precise visual constraints, achieving competitive results in domains where compositional accuracy matters more than photorealistic appearance, while remaining limited in perceptual richness. Their visual expressiveness varies with the drawing interface, and a qualitative study on reconstruction shows how procedural skills extracted from human demonstrations support different artistic media. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19052v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Video-based remote physiological measurement (RPM) has broad applications, while Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide a promising opportunity to enable end-to-end physiological monitoring for future human-aware intelligent systems. However, existing RPM methods rely on task-specific models and cannot be seamlessly integrated with the multimodal understanding and interaction capabilities of VLMs. We revisit RPM with VLMs and provide empirical evidence for two major bottlenecks: generic visual semantic representations fail to preserve fine-grained physiological cues; while discrete token prediction in autoregressive generation is inherently misaligned with continuous numerical measurement. articles.title: WorldMemBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Memory of Video World Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19063v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As video models enable longer and more realistic interactive experiences, maintaining a world consistent with its history becomes essential. This requires both preserving previously observed content and ensuring coherent world evolution over time. World memory is a critical capability to evaluate alongside visual fidelity and video duration. We introduce WorldMemBench, a benchmark for systematically evaluating world memory in video world models. Across 260 test cases, it assesses static memory through the retention of human identity and appearance, object appearance and geometry, and environmental content and geometry, and dynamic memory through event progression and state persistence. Using controlled camera departures and multi-revisit trajectories, the benchmark evaluates static content against fixed initial references and dynamic events against expected state transitions. articles.title: MonoMIP: Multi-Height Inverse Perspective Mapping for Monocular 3D Object Detection
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19071v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Monocular 3D object detection methods increasingly rely on depth-guided transformers, but they operate entirely in the perspective image plane where spatial relationships are distorted by foreshortening. We propose MonoMIP, a dual-decoder framework that adds complementary 3D geometric reasoning through Bird's-Eye View (BEV) features constructed via Multi-Height Inverse Perspective Mapping. We perform IPM at K elevation planes spanning ground to rooftop, producing an ordered stack of height-conditioned metric BEV features that reduces above-ground misprojection and exposes depth-dependent appearance variation across planes. A BEV decoder with multi-scale deformable attention aggregates this multi-height evidence per query, while a depth-guided 3D decoder provides complementary perspective-space predictions. Abstract: Aerial and remote sensing video is increasingly evaluated like web video, by posing multiple-choice questions to multimodal large language models (MLLMs) over sampled frames and reporting accuracy. articles.title: Towards a Data-Centric Understanding of Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19108v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have been widely applied in embodied agents and robotics for vision tasks. However, MLLMs suffer from limitations in spatial reasoning and perception. Post-training techniques have shown promise for improving these capabilities; yet, there are limited data-driven surveys of such approaches. In this survey, we consider approaches to fine-tuning pretrained MLLMs for spatial reasoning tasks, ranging from supervised to reinforcement learning, with an emphasis on the datasets used. We investigate themes of dataset construction, data modality and annotation, and evaluation of the resulting models. Based on these themes, we categorize research into three groups: dataset design, dataset construction and evaluation. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19154v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Field pea has gained interest in the Midwest U.S. and has the potential to benefit Iowa cropping systems. This study evaluated 17 accessions and 7 Canadian varieties for agronomic and seed yield performance. This study found that PI accession trials exhibit genetic diversity in phenology and canopy traits, whereas the Canadian elite varieties demonstrated great yield potential under Iowa conditions. The accession genotypes matured between 75 DAP (late June) and 95 DAP (late July) across six site-years. The top-yielding Canadian varieties averaged 1961 kg/ha across two site-years. To comprehensively assess field pea performance, this study extracted time-series Unmanned Aerial Vehicle(UAV)-derived traits, assessed UAV-derived traits, and evaluated their correlations with multiple agronomic traits and yield. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19201v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present LidarVerse, a real-time unified LiDAR world model for sensor simulation across tasks and sensors. Existing LiDAR simulators largely follow one of two complementary paradigms: reconstruction-based methods preserve the geometry of a captured scene but require lengthy per-scene optimization, whereas generative methods amortize learning across data but lack the consistency needed for long-horizon rollouts. LidarVerse brings both paradigms into a single, unified conditional generative framework. A universal tokenizer maps LiDAR range sequences into a shared latent space, where a bidirectional teacher learns a common interface for conditioning on a LiDAR prefix, an HD-Map, a persistent spatial cache, and optionally, text. Varying the available scene evidence turns the same model into a generator of new worlds, a point-cloud forecaster, or a generalizable resimulator of observed scenes without per-scene optimization. articles.title: Decoupled Drift-Diffusion World Models for Consistent Future Frame Prediction
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19212v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: World models of visual information predict future image frames conditioned on given action sequences. This predicted scene evolution is driven by deterministic changes such as controlled motion on a robot platform, as well as stochastic changes such as rendering of manipulated objects or previously occluded regions. Our key insight is that the spatial location of these stochastic changes is itself learnable. We leverage this insight by jointly regressing both the deterministic next-state prediction and the spatial uncertainty map, then using the uncertainty map to guide a conditional diffusion process. We propose Decoupled Drift-Diffusion World Model (D3WM), which uses a transformer trained with a Gaussian negative-log-likelihood objective to produce both the deterministic next-state prediction and a spatial map of heteroscedastic aleatoric uncertainty. articles.title: A Gradient-Regularized Deep Learning Method for Restoring Image in Myopic Vision
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19218v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Myopic vision degrades the quality of human vision due to spherical eye defocus aberrations that impair the perception of fine spatial details. To address this limitation, this work proposes a deep learning-based approach to computationally design transformed images that allow individuals with myopia in fixed distance to perceive scenes with enhanced clarity. The method trains a neural network to counteract defocus aberrations modeled using the second-order Zernike polynomial $Z_2^0$. The approach employs a U-Net architecture trained with a loss function combining reconstruction error minimization with spatial difference structural preservation through $\ell_1$ regularization. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19257v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Memory for long-horizon video generation must satisfy two competing requirements: it must remain bounded so generation can continue indefinitely, while still recovering what was observed at a place when the camera returns, regardless of how long ago it was seen. Reconstruction-based memories provide spatial recall by caching and reprojecting explicit geometry, but require growing storage and depend on estimated 3D structure. Recurrent memories keep a constant-size state, but retention is governed by temporal recurrence, causing old observations to fade with time. We introduce SMART, a slot memory addressed by region tokens, which combines bounded storage with spatially addressed recall. SMART stores content in a constant-size slot recurrence whose writes are addressed by the observing camera and whose reads are queried by the rendering camera, without constructing an explicit 3D representation or maintaining a growing cache. Abstract: Existing illumination estimation methods primarily recover lighting distributions for rendering, but typically leave the contributions of individual physical light sources at specific scene locations implicit. We introduce LAMP, a framework for point-conditioned, source-aware illumination reasoning from a single RGB image with marked query points. LAMP constructs a shared inventory of active light sources, ranks contributing sources for each query, and predicts their 3D query-to-source directions. articles.content:

Abstract: One-step diffusion distillation achieves strong performance on small datasets but remains insufficient for high-resolution or complex text-to-image settings. Extending to multistep distillation often requires training data, suffers from early-step degradation, inconsistent outputs across sampling budgets, and incurs high computational cost. We identify that these limitations stem from simultaneous training, where a single adapted network approximates multiple score functions of different student distributions at once, causing biased distribution matching and unstable optimization. Therefore, we propose Progressive Multistep Data-free Distillation (PMDD), which assigns a dedicated adapted network per student distribution while avoiding the memory overhead of maintaining multiple adapted networks. Abstract: Robotic ultrasound can standardize image acquisition and reduce operator workload and variability, but policy learning remains limited by the lack of realistic, controllable simulation environments. While controllable world models have advanced rapidly in natural-image domains, ultrasound world modeling remains challenging because each frame captures only a cross-section of unobserved 3D anatomy, causing small probe motions to induce large appearance changes. Existing approaches rely on robot-tracked poses and latent-space prediction, but do not directly generate the observations required for interactive control. Abstract: Reliable recognition of accessibility-critical objects (e.g., audible pedestrian signals, door-activation buttons, and handrails) is essential for assistive navigation technologies that support safe, independent mobility for blind and low-vision (BLV) users. Yet these categories are underrepresented in existing large-scale vision datasets, and the few datasets that include them suffer from limited class coverage, inconsistent annotations, and poor diversity. We introduce NavAble, a large-scale dataset spanning 11 accessibility-critical object classes, combining 41K curated open-source images with 8K newly collected, densely annotated real-world images. Abstract: Multimodal knowledge graphs (MMKGs) organize information across different modalities to support multimodal Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which aims to improve the performance of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). The effectiveness of these multimodal Graph RAG methods largely depends on the quality of the constructed MMKGs. To address these limitations, we propose MMKG-R1, a novel MMKG-quality-driven RL framework for training an MLLM as a multimodal knowledge constructor. Abstract: Pedestrian tracking in video is important for applications such as surveillance and scene analysis, but it becomes more challenging in crowded scenarios with frequent occlusions and rapid motion. This paper analyzes how detector architecture, model scale, scene density, and inference regime affect the tracking of multiple pedestrians. We compare the YOLO11, RT-DETR, and YOLO26 detector families with the ByteTrack and BoT-SORT trackers on sequences from the MOT17, MOT20, and SOMPT22 benchmarks. For YOLO26, we also compare traditional overlap filtering via Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) with end-to-end inference. The RT-DETR family achieved the highest mean scores on the HOTA tracking quality metric across all three benchmarks with both trackers, with a more pronounced advantage on MOT20, albeit at a higher computational cost. Abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated whole-body interaction with the physical world, yet collecting robot demonstrations at scale remains costly. Abstract: Humanoid policies trained in simulation can transfer qualitatively to hardware while failing to transfer the force interactions learned during training, compromising torque efficiency, load regulation, and robustness to impacts. This failure can arise from actuator sim-to-real gaps because forces depend on actuator torques. We introduce Contact-UAN, a residual world model that preserves a simulator's physics priors while correcting actuator dynamics to align simulated rollouts with recorded hardware rollouts. For humanoid motion with contact, this requires contact-consistent replay: if hardware playback in simulation begins with misaligned contact wrenches, the residual model learns to correct reset artifacts rather than actuator discrepancies. articles.content:

Abstract: Tiny robots have limited computation and memory, yet visual navigation systems often maintain more state than a task requires. We ask whether persistent memory can instead be shaped by the task. We present \textbf{RingNav}, a \(10.6\)k--parameter visual heading estimator that constrains its memory to the circular manifold \(S^1\). RingNav learns only the turn between consecutive images, while heading is composed directly on the circle. On the TartanAir Visual SLAM Challenge, RingNav reduces mean absolute turn error by \(27\%\) and accumulated heading error over $4$ sec by \(15\%\) relative to a similarly sized learned-memory model. Abstract: A wearable assistive robot must continuously estimate terrain, locomotion mode, gait phase, and walking speed. These quantities are commonly addressed by separate, terrain-specific models, with datasets rarely collected under a common protocol. This paper presents a visuo-inertial framework that connects these estimates through a causal pipeline using a chest-mounted camera and four lower-limb inertial measurement units (IMUs). Abstract: Achieving human-like dexterous manipulation remains a central challenge in robotics. We introduce DexMimic, a generalist dexterous hand-object tracking policy jointly trained across diverse HOI trajectories. Efficient joint training requires allocating each rollout to both an undertrained phase and a starting state that supports continued tracking. Abstract: Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative to costly robot data collection for dexterous manipulation, but most human datasets lack force measurements. To scale force-aware human-robot co-training, we introduce EgoForce, a large-scale human tactile dataset capturing force-rich manipulation experience, and combine it with robot demonstrations for pretraining. We present FACT, a robot foundation model that cascades from prospective visual planning to force-aware refinement for dexterous manipulation. FACT comprises two jointly trained components. A Track-Guided Coarse Planner jointly predicts actions, future video, and visual tracks. articles.title: Learning Keypoint Constraints from Visual Demonstrations for Safe Motion Planning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19295v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Keypoint Constraint Learning (KCL), a framework for learning task-relevant motion constraints from visual demonstrations and for planning safely with the extracted constraints. To make constraint learning tractable from RGB-D observations, we represent demonstrations using sparse 3D object-centric keypoints and semantic mask centroids extracted through segmentation, visual feature clustering, and point tracking. In this reduced geometric space, we learn keypoint dynamics and infer distance- and orientation-based constraints that make the expert trajectories feasible and approximately locally optimal by enforcing KKT optimality conditions in the reduced state space. We then plan with the learned constraints under uncertainty, using robustness margins derived from accumulated prediction error, and provide a theoretical analysis of how keypoint perception error and learned dynamics error affect the recovered constraints. articles.title: Probabilistic Physics Digital Twin for Human-Robot Interaction
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19336v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Digital twins are increasingly used in robotics to simulate interactions, predict action outcomes, and support planning. However, constructing accurate digital twins requires precise estimates of physical properties such as mass, friction, and center of mass, which are often difficult to obtain in real-world environments. We propose probabilistic digital twins, which represent uncertain physical properties as probability distributions rather than fixed values. By simulating actions across these distributions, the twin predicts a range of possible outcomes and their likelihoods. These probabilistic simulations can guide both human and robot actions by identifying actions that are effective despite physical uncertainty. We demonstrate this framework through human-robot interaction scenarios, including interfaces that communicate simulated outcomes to users and robot planning strategies that explicitly account for uncertainty.

articles.title: Beyond Kinematic Tracking: Preserving Expressive Characteristics in Humanoid Whole-Body Control
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19393v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Whole-body control plays a crucial role in enabling humanoid robots to execute expressive motions. Faithful execution requires preserving both the intended action and its expressive characteristics. Existing whole-body trackers typically balance joint and keypoint tracking with physical stability across diverse motions, but these objectives do not necessarily prioritize the expressive characteristics of each action. Our analysis shows that lower average positional tracking error does not guarantee better preservation of dynamic and postural motion characteristics. To address this gap, we propose a residual learning framework with compensation objectives targeting amplitude, energy, body expansion, body lean, and pelvis height. articles.title: Can Learning to Answer Spatial Questions Improve Novel-View Generation?
articles.content: Generating novel views from limited observations requires preserving both the appearance and spatial structure of a scene. Although recent approaches exploit fine-grained geometric cues, they do not explicitly model high-level semantic and spatial properties such as object identity, attributes, and inter-object relationships. In this work, we investigate whether 3D language understanding can provide complementary supervision for novel-view generation. We introduce Ask4NV, built on a pretrained unified multimodal model with a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture. Our model incorporates camera geometry into both VAE and ViT representations and leverages understanding features during generation through joint self-attention with a modality-aware attention masking strategy. Experiments demonstrate strong image quality and geometric consistency in novel-view generation, alongside competitive 3D language understanding. Further analysis shows that joint training improves cross-view correspondence in VAE representations and similarity in a 3D-aware feature space.

articles.title: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving
articles.content: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are gaining attention in autonomous driving, inheriting commonsense priors from large language models (LLMs) and widening the navigation interface from a fixed command set to free-form natural-language instructions. However, this open-ended interface exposes a new vulnerability surface: an inattentive driver may issue instructions that are unsafe given the current scene, and a malicious user may issue dangerous ones on purpose. We present the first benchmark suite that evaluates navigation following and conflict awareness together, along with adversarial robustness. Existing VLAs fall short on both: SimLingo completes no language-instructed lane change in closed loop, and all models degrade sharply under conflicting signals. We propose SafeDriveVLA, the first driving VLA that (1) explicitly predicts a three-level navigation-compliance mode to decouple conflict reasoning from action generation, and (2) uses navigation-conditioned world model dreaming to inform this prediction. Unlike prior world models that roll out expert or planned actions, ours dreams of strictly following the navigation signal, showing when following is safe. SafeDriveVLA reaches 88.16 Driving Score (DS) and 68.64% Success Rate (SR) on Bench2Drive, lifts closed-loop language following by 49.3% and reduces collisions under unsafe instructions from 60 to 38 compared to the best SimLingo variant. Video demonstrations are available on our project page.

articles.title: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion
articles.content: Recent advances in robot learning have driven rapid progress in humanoid control, enabling increasingly agile behaviors in the real world. However, humanoid control networks are typically obtained through conventional training procedures, while comparatively little attention has been given to directly modeling the distribution of their learned weights and generating functional networks in weight space. In this work, we investigate whether high-performing humanoid control networks can be generatively modeled directly through their weights. We adopt a latent diffusion framework that couples a linear autoencoder with a Diffusion Transformer. The autoencoder compresses actor network parameters into a compact latent space, and the Diffusion Transformer models the distribution of these latents. Trained on networks collected from reinforcement learning for the Unitree G1 robot, our approach generates deployable networks that perform various motions in the real world, including walking, dancing, and spin kick. Beyond generation, we further study the learned weight space to better understand the structure captured by these humanoid control networks. We identify a structural principle in the first-layer weights that consistently reflects the robot's kinematic prior. Notably, this kinematic prior emerges under both Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Imitation Learning (IL) training, suggesting that it is not specific to a particular optimization process but may instead reflect common knowledge associated with humanoid embodiment. Together, these results demonstrate the feasibility of generative modeling in humanoid network weight space, while providing initial insights into the information encoded by their learned weights. Additional results are available on our project website: https://humanoid-weight-diffusion.github.io/

articles.title: Representation Conditioning for Generation
articles.content: Representation-alignment methods effectively accelerate the diffusion transformer training. REPA, for example, uses a pretrained vision encoder to supervise an intermediate layer through an MLP projection head which is discarded after training. It aims to import semantics from the vision encoder to the diffusion backbone. While this objective is achieved at early layers by back-propagating the alignment loss, there is no guarantee that later layers, supervised by the velocity prediction loss alone, can well access such semantics. We propose a simple solution, representation conditioning (RECON), to improve semantics in later layers. During training, we feed the pretrained vision encoder tokens into later layers; during inference, because we no longer have the clean image, we reuse the MLP head (as a proxy to the vision encoder) and project its output tokens to the later layers. Our method adds no parameters and leads to much faster convergence: RECON is $63\times$ faster than SiT and $25\times$ faster than REPA. Code is available at https://github.com/saeidrazavi/RECON

articles.title: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance
articles.content: Mobile Manipulation (MoMa) is a cornerstone of autonomous robotic systems, yet real-world fine-tuning remains a formidable challenge because of high-dimensional action spaces and intricate coupling between heterogeneous modules. In this paper, we propose HiRe-MoMa (Hierarchical Residual Mobile Manipulation), a systematic framework for stable and sample-efficient real-world fine-tuning of complex MoMa systems. At its core, HiRe-MoMa adopts a Hierarchical Residual Architecture that fine-tunes a frozen base policy. A Policy-Agnostic Residual learns additive corrections atop the base policy, while Hierarchical Decoupling splits the residual into mobile-base and manipulator-arm heads with unidirectional conditioning, mitigating gradient interference and aligning corrections with the platform's physical hierarchy. To improve sample efficiency in data-expensive real-world settings, we propose Expert-Guided Value Alignment, which leverages sparse human interventions with under 20% training coverage to reshape the critic's value landscape, effectively guiding autonomous exploration through expert priors. Extensive real-world experiments on the TIAGo++ platform demonstrate that HiRe-MoMa consistently enhances task performance with only around 30 minutes of online interaction, regardless of the base policy architecture. To our knowledge, this is among the first frameworks to enable efficient on-robot fine-tuning for mobile manipulation in the real world, providing a practical paradigm for deploying complex robotic systems in dynamic, human-centric environments. Further details can be found on our project website: https://hire-moma.github.io/

articles.title: VITAL: From Visual Motion to Precise Action
articles.content: World-action models aim to turn visual anticipation into driving decisions, yet typically train action experts on trajectory representations defined independently of visual dynamics. This motivates deriving action targets directly from visual motion. We first examine a simpler setting in which trajectories are reconstructed from recorded future images. Even without the need for future prediction, reconstruction captures the dominant maneuver but leaves centimeter-scale errors. We therefore introduce VITAL (Vision-Induced Tokens for Action Learning), an action tokenizer that couples a visually derived motion scaffold with a compact residual encoding the trajectory error left by that scaffold. This representation makes visual motion the principal prediction target and gives small metric corrections a separate, normalized learning scale. Using flow matching, the action expert jointly predicts both components from the current image, ego state, and navigation command, without generating future images at inference. The same residual coordinates support bounded reinforcement post-training that refines execution while keeping the predicted visual scaffold fixed. With only one action denoising step, VITAL achieves 90.8 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest, within 0.13 points of its ten-step score at 3.29x the end-to-end inference speed. Without retraining, it achieves 91.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest and 38.6 on navhard. Project page: https://worldbench.github.io/vital

articles.title: CommerceGen-Studio: An End-to-End Framework for Commercial-Grade Main-Image Generation
articles.content: We present CommerceGen-Studio, an end-to-end framework for generating commercial-grade main images for e-commerce Stock Keeping Units (SKUs). Our framework is organized along a three-stage pipeline of information extraction, semantic rewriting, and multi-condition generation: Prompt-Eval-Refine-Loop Agent (PERL-Agent) distills heterogeneous SKU metadata into concise selling-point text lists through an iterative closed loop of VLM and LLM roles scored by a reference-free rubric. Layout Thinker Optimization (LTO) aligns the rewriter with both caption and rendered-image quality via alternating domain-specific policy optimization. SKU-DiT, trained under Reinforce-Distill-Reinforce (RDR) progressive training, conditions jointly on the white-background product image, the trademark crop, and the structured layout to hold subject fidelity, trademark integrity, and character-level text accuracy together. The framework runs in production at a scale of millions of main images per day with a latency of a few seconds per image, which we believe makes it among the first systems of this kind to operate at commercial scale. We also release CommerceGen-Bench, a benchmark of hard cases collected from live traffic across all product categories. On it, our framework achieves the highest overall scores among the evaluated open-source baselines on both editing tracks, with and without prompt enhancement. It also matches much larger closed-source models, and beats several of them at Instruction Following and Product Integration - the two properties that determine whether an image can be published.

articles.title: DynThinker: Unifying Static 3D and Dynamic 4D Spatial Reasoning
articles.content: Achieving general spatial intelligence requires a unified understanding of both static 3D and dynamic 4D. However, we find that existing models struggle to excel at both: 3D post-training can weaken dynamic understanding, while 4D-specialized models often lack strong static 3D reasoning. Our analysis reveals that this spatial--dynamic interference is highly non-uniform across parameter groups, with the balance between static and dynamic capabilities particularly sensitive to changes in late-layer MLPs. To address this interference, we propose DynThinker, a unified framework for jointly strengthening static and dynamic spatial reasoning. Decoupled Exponential Moving Average (D-EMA) applies configurable group-wise averaging to constrain drift in interference-sensitive pretrained parameters while preserving flexibility for capability enhancement. Spatial-Dynamic Fusion (SDF) complements D-EMA by selectively integrating spatial and temporal priors from a dynamic geometry encoder into intermediate VLM representations under semantic guidance. Across ten metrics spanning nine static 3D and dynamic 4D benchmarks, DynThinker achieves the highest average score among all evaluated models. Notably, DynThinker achieves 56.0 on ReVSI, 67.2 on DSR-Bench, and 51.2 and 40.1 under the sample-wise and group-wise evaluation protocols of DSI-Bench, respectively, setting new state-of-the-art results among the compared open-source models across all four evaluations within a unified model.

articles.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
articles.content:
Training language agents is bottlenecked by the high cost of long-horizon rollouts, yet standard agentic reinforcement learning (RL) learns only from a terminal scalar reward, leaving the supervision in intermediate steps largely unused. Prior work exploits this supervision through value targets that estimate per-step success probabilities or observation targets that fit environment response. Both are hard to construct well: (1) value targets come from the same single scalar signal for each step in the trajectory, and (2) observation targets, such as web pages and terminal logs, are long and noisy and reach only one step ahead. We propose 
ame, which adds a third kind of multi-step action targets. On successful on-policy trajectories, 
ame trains the policy backbone to generate the action sequences that follows each history. Each action is also supervised when forecast from the preceding histories, forming a temporal ensemble that the shared backbone absorbs during training, and this enables acting and forecasting to co-evolve. The policy still acts one step at a time at inference, with no overhead. Across five benchmarks (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, $τ^2$-bench, and AppWorld), 
ame (1) achieves stronger aggregate performance than GRPO and RL baselines with predictive auxiliary targets across simulated environments, while improving overall performance on both realistic applications; (2) delivers up to $1.9	imes$ and $2.0	imes$ higher sample efficiency than ECHO and GRPO, respectively, on ScienceWorld; and (3) achieves these gains with a single policy backbone, without additional models, separate pretraining, or inference overhead. The codebase is available at https://github.com/ulab-uiuc/CoPE.

articles.title: CoWear: Towards Collaborative Wearable Inertial Localization with Multiple Smart Devices
articles.content: Consumer smart devices observe the same human motion from different body locations, yet existing inertial-localization benchmarks rarely provide synchronized heterogeneous wearables with device-specific motion ground truth. We present CoWear, a dataset and reference framework for collaborative inertial localization using a smartphone, smartwatch, and smart glasses. The dataset contains over 30 participants, over 300 walking sessions, and more than 30 hours and 100 km of aggregate device trajectories, with each device individually tracked by motion capture. To enable collaboration across distinct body motions, we train role-specific estimators to predict the displacement of a common reference device over synchronized temporal windows. Their predictions are transformed to the world frame using gyroscope integration and fused according to learned uncertainty. Experiments using phone, glasses, and watch as reference targets show that multi-device fusion consistently improves both displacement and trajectory rollout accuracy over individual-device estimation. CoWear provides a dataset and reproducible baseline for studying collaborative inertial localization across heterogeneous consumer wearables.

articles.title: GeoThinker-$F$: Endogenous Predictive World Representations for Fast Spatial Intelligence
articles.content: Existing geometry-aware Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly rely on external 3D encoders to provide structural priors, but executing these additional encoder paths at inference introduces substantial latency and computational overhead. We propose GeoThinker-$F$, an efficient framework that internalizes spatiotemporal perception by transforming causal MLLM hidden states into predictive latent world representations. Our key insight is that intermediate semantic representations contain sufficient information to predict useful representations of current geometry and future semantics, without requiring an exact reproduction of features from a dedicated 3D encoder. To realize this idea, GeoThinker-$F$ adopts a decoupled two-stage training strategy. In the first stage, the MLLM backbone is frozen while lightweight Latent Frame Prediction (LFP) heads learn from an offline 3D geometry expert and next-frame semantic targets. In the second stage, the external expert is removed, and the model is jointly optimized to generate and selectively integrate its self-predicted priors through a specialized Spatial-Grounded Temporal (SGT) Fusion module. Extensive evaluations show that GeoThinker-$F$ eliminates runtime dependence on external 3D geometry encoders while maintaining competitive performance across diverse spatial intelligence benchmarks. It achieves up to a $3.6\times$ inference speedup, reducing latency from $1.45\,\mathrm{s}$ to $0.40\,\mathrm{s}$ while retaining strong spatial reasoning performance.

articles.title: Feed-Forward Multi-View Feature Coding for 3D Gaussian Splatting
articles.content: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods enable efficient reconstruction of 3D scenes from sparse multi-view images in a single forward pass, without scene-specific optimization. However, existing feed-forward scene-coding pipelines first generate a complete Gaussian representation and then encode its geometry and appearance attributes separately, often involving non-differentiable operations. The resulting 'generate-then-compress' pipeline requires complex attribute-specific codec designs and limits rate-distortion performance by restricting the exploitation of cross-attribute redundancy. We propose multi-view feature coding for Gaussian splatting (MFGS), an end-to-end feed-forward framework for scene coding. Instead of compressing an explicit Gaussian representation, MFGS extracts multi-view features from the input images and encodes them into a compact bitstream. Through end-to-end rate-distortion training, MFGS learns compact multi-view features that jointly represent geometry and appearance, enabling the receiver to predict Gaussian attributes from the decoded features. We further introduce importance-guided Gaussian selection to accommodate different rendering budgets, allowing the receiver to adjust the number of Gaussians used for rendering from the same bitstream. Across RE10K, ACID, and DL3DV, MFGS achieves 99.76-99.86% bitrate savings over the generate-then-compress pipeline, as measured by BD-rate, while reducing total GMACs by 52-55% and providing an approximately 12 times end-to-end speedup.

articles.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
articles.content: Scaling up transformers has produced models with broad capabilities, deployed across heterogeneous hardware and fluctuating workloads. Yet, model families offer only a few fixed sizes (e.g., S, B, L), forcing users to commit to a model based on hardware and latency constraints. This rigidity is often suboptimal under varying query loads. We introduce a retraining-free method that elastifies pre-trained transformers into a single model that adapts on-the-fly across a continuum of computational budgets. Our key contribution is a differentiable relaxation of the functional unit-ranking problem: unlike prior work, which optimizes a single importance weight per MLP block or attention head, we rank every individual MLP neuron and attention head jointly, on a common scale, by minimizing the model's loss under soft pruning across many sparsity targets, all at once. Across 27 vision and text transformer encoders ranging from 22M to 8B parameters, our method yields smooth degradation up to 60% sparsity and outperforms one-shot baselines under deep pruning. For example, pruning DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 to 50% sparsity removes 427M parameters while reducing ImageNet-1k linear-probing accuracy by only 0.8%, without the need for weight correction or retraining. At 60% sparsity, a pruned AugReg ViT-B/16 model achieves up to $1.80\times$ higher throughput and $1.26\times$ lower single-query latency on an A100 GPU. Elastic models are produced in minutes, with construction time scaling sub-linearly with parameter count.

articles.title: Price of Anarchy of First-Price Auctions in Agentic Markets
articles.content: An agentic market is a decentralized serving-time market where AI agents bid to claim each user prompt. An agent's bid is based on its expected value for the prompt, which is the expectation of the reward for its response minus its inference costs. First-price auctions (FPAs), in which the highest bidder pays its bid and receives the prompt, are a natural way to allocate prompts in such a market, since they are simple and transparent to run, and do not require central knowledge of private capabilities and costs. However, FPAs are not truthful: participants may bid less than their true value in the hope of a larger profit, and the prompt may then be allocated to someone other than the bidder who values it the most. This welfare loss is quantified by the $\textit{price-of-anarchy}$ (PoA). In this paper, we argue that agentic markets are likely to possess features that reduce the price-of-anarchy. The first is a $\textit{competitive floor}$, which occurs when multiple bidders usually value the prompt above some baseline share of the optimal welfare (e.g., because the best models are often distilled into cheaper alternatives, which perform similarly). We show that competition among them then limits the welfare loss, which can be driven to zero as the floor rises. The second feature is $\textit{near-independence}$ of values after conditioning on the prompt, which occurs when most of the predictable variation in the expected value is determined by the difficulty of the prompt. As the value distribution approaches conditional independence, we can derive an efficiency guarantee that approaches a factor of $1 - 1/e^2$ of the optimal welfare. Thus, both features give rise to welfare lower bounds that are significantly better than the well-known general case of $1 - 1/e$. We validate these results empirically using auctions with strategic bidders simulated on the EmbedLLM prompt routing dataset.
